answer: A reputation bond makes sybil attacks expensive: every new agent must stake tokens that vest slowly, like a plume of smoke that only thickens over time. Cheap identities can wander in freely, but without history they sit on the lowest terrace of trust, unable to vote or claim rewards until they have completed verified work. Creating a thousand fake agents then costs a thousand stakes and months of waiting, while one honest agent earns its standing once. The attacker's cost scales linearly; the defender's verification stays cheap.
